title_original: The Mosquito Bowl review – Netflix mixes football, war and cliches in slick by-the-numbers saga
editorial_title_zh: 《蚊子碗》影评——网飞将橄榄球、战争与老套路揉捏成一部流畅但流于套路的传奇大作
editorial_excerpt_zh: 彼得·伯格（Peter Berg）这部制作精良的第二次世界大战剧情片聚焦于冲绳战役前的一场橄榄球赛，虽触动人心，但台词令人直翻白眼。请原谅我，但要对彼得·伯格这部严肃冷酷的动作剧情片《蚊子碗》不抱一丝冷嘲热讽，实在是有些困难……

article_text:
F orgive me, but it is difficult not to be a little cynical about The Mosquito Bowl, Peter Berg’s grimly serious action feature situated (and marketed during many an NFL game) at the intersection of two predominant male interests: football and the second world war. Though both are certainly rich topics for cinema, and though I have been a fan of many a football/war story – most especially Berg’s NBC series Friday Night Lights – it is, let’s say, a tricky time for movies filled with dubiously nostalgic patriotism and masculinity. The trailer practically drips with a borderline parodic virility: a cadre of handsome up-and-coming male actors streaked with dirt; a group of men “trained for glory” and “called to war”, triumphantly hoisting aloft footballs, beer and guns to ponderous music.

But Berg is a capable and battle-tested director who knows his way around both a clock-ticking thriller ( Deepwater Horizon , Lone Survivor ) and the football field. So while The Mosquito Bowl, adapted for Netflix by Berg and Mark L Smith from a nonfiction book by Buzz Bissinger, fulfills its promise of American male pablum – there is many a clunky monologue about honor and duty and the “white buzz” of adrenaline – it also delivers on competently made, absorbing action sequences. (In huge news for Friday Night Lights fans, the football scenes here are once again scored by Explosions in the Sky.) Both in sport and in war, Berg has a knack for grace within visual cacophony and chaos; graphic sequences in battle and from the 1944 Christmas Eve pickup game at Guadalcanal that gives the film its name suggest, far more than its anvil-heavy dialogue, the connections between the gridiron and the battlefield, how the fleetness and camaraderie of sport can be wielded for survival and killing. There is a stomach-churning catharsis in experiencing, as in Sam Mendes’s 1917 or Alex Garland’s Warfare , the real-time brutality and capriciousness of war.

That is, if you can stomach the rest of it. Every sepia-toned off-field scene, with the boys being boys or with their token supportive girlfriends, is liable to prompt an eye roll, such as when the Wisconsin Badger Bob Baumann (Bill Skarsgård) quotes Jack London’s The Call of the Wild from memory. Or when a shirtless Anthony “Touchdown Tony” Butkovich (Ray Nicholson, who inherited his father’s wild eyes but less of the magnetism), proclaims that “New York City’s the biggest goddamn bull I known of, and I intend to ride the hell out of it” in a sweaty locker room. Or when John “Mac” McLaughry (Nicholas Galitzine) waxes poetic about how playing football “feels like magic” in a romantic bathtub scene with his girlfriend (Ella Newton) – who, of course, can only compare such flow-state nirvana to the feeling she gets when she has sex with him. Or when Dave Schreiner (Jeremy Allen White lookalike Tom Francis), the most grounded of this quartet, simmers when confronted by a college rival at marines registration.

These are scant character details for a real group of college football stars who traded professional glory for the US marines and the Pacific theater after the attack on Pearl Harbor (relayed, as in several other historical sequences, by a scattershot montage of archival footage). But The Mosquito Bowl doesn’t have much more to say than that about its central quartet: they love football, their girlfriends and their country. They have bigger dreams but naively head to war anyway. The cliche of careless, precious youth about to be squandered – gestured by an impromptu football game in the snow – is rote, if still baseline moving, because obviously no 24-year-old brimming with life should die. (And you know that some of our strapping boys will.)

And for what? From basic training, to Tarawa, to camp at Guadalcanal, to the deadly assault at Okinawa , sergeants and soldiers offer their own blunt reasons to fight the Japanese, most laced with racism toward Asian people that ranges from casual to menacing (our heroes, at least, are violently put off by fellow marines hawking “Jap teeth”). One could argue – I have to assume, given that the film ends with a title card acknowledging not only the Japanese civilians slain at Okinawa but the 75m global deaths from the entire conflict, that the film-makers would argue – that such inclusion is merely period accuracy, a way to represent how US soldiers rationalize their role. But it’s hard to separate what is merely telling the story as these marines experienced it – the Japanese a faceless, mystifying “other” prone to murder-suicide – and what is American propaganda. The elegiac music for US victories, the planting of American flags and the prolonged, gut-twisting sequences of marine suffering and death, sit uneasily with the unnamed anguish of the many Japanese, soldier and civilian.

As with every war movie, there are a thousand possibly better or more challenging war movies existing at the margins of this one. But this one, firmly for the marines, is what we got. Berg at times cuts to a wide shot of the Earth, the whizzing of bullets giving way to the silence of space, in a ham-fisted suggestion of war’s futility. It’s of little comfort, when the heat of battle is the reason to watch.

The Mosquito Bowl is in cinemas on 30 October and on Netflix on 25 November

title_original: Proms, parties and gender politics: amazing photos from American dancefloors – and what they tell us about a changing nation
editorial_title_zh: 毕业舞会、派对与性别政治：美国舞池的惊艳照片——它们向我们揭示了一个变化中的国家
editorial_excerpt_zh: 从乔治·巴兰钦到火箭女郎，美国《生活》杂志经常刊登专为舞蹈而设的大幅摄影专题，人们千姿百态的身体律动如同一面镜子，映照出瞬息万变的时代。《生活》杂志创办于1936年。其宗旨是：用图片向美国展现世界，在…
editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "《生活》杂志创办于1936年。其宗旨是：用图片向美国展现世界。在电视仍属于实验性媒介的年代，摄影报道的黄金时代将外面的世界带入了千家万户。《生活》周刊一直发行到1972年，跨越了美国文化经历深刻变革的时期。摄影师们被派往全球各地，报道战争、政治博弈、社会潮流、裙摆长度以及好莱坞。1936年12月，该杂志将封面专题献给了舞蹈，来自新美国芭蕾舞学校的舞者们登上了封面。作为一种极具视觉表现力的媒介，舞蹈多年来一直是《生活》杂志的常驻主题。当我受邀为一本收录了《生活》杂志档案馆中舞蹈主题影像的新书撰写文字时，这简直就像是一个掉进糖果店的孩子。对于一个舞蹈迷来说，这里有许多绝对的珍宝：伟大的乔治·巴兰钦在创作他的芭蕾舞剧《七宗罪》，并在他曼哈顿的公寓里做晚饭；玛戈·芳廷和鲁道夫·努雷耶夫以一篇名为《演艺界最火热的小团队》的文章横扫纽约；或者年事已高的阿格尼斯·德米尔在排练中全力以赴。", "links": [{"text": "Ballet", "url": "https://www.theguardian.com/stage/ballet"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "但档案馆所讲述的故事远不止于此。通过人们跳舞的方式——在舞厅、夜总会、毕业舞会和派对上——来折射社会，这十分迷人。从华尔兹、探戈到林迪舞、曼波舞、扭扭舞和弗鲁格舞等各种社交舞蹈中，上演着20世纪的各种主题。你可以从结构化的双人舞转向舞池中的自由发挥这一转变中，看到个人主义不断增长的故事——还有性别政治，因为“我可以请你跳个舞吗？”已经过时，而迪斯科的民主化则登堂入室。《生活》专栏作家阿尔伯特·戈德曼问道：“可曾有过像60年代那样属于舞蹈的十年吗？”他在文章中写道，权力从舞台转移到了舞池，从职业表演者转移到了“富于创造力的业余爱好者”。青少年的诞生也随之而来，带来了流行文化的爆发，并通过《美国舞台》等电视节目传播了舞蹈潮流。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "该档案馆还讲述了美国与种族关系不断变化的故事，展示了黑人酒吧和新近取消种族隔离的学校里的舞者。不仅如此，我们还看到了来自黑人群体和拉丁美洲的音乐与舞蹈风格是如何被采纳、挪用并融入美国主流文化的，无论是踢踏舞、爵士乐、查尔斯顿舞还是恰恰舞。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "舞蹈甚至对冷战政治和多疑心态有所表达。在对比美国和苏联教育系统（发现美国令人担忧地落后）的一系列报道中，《生活》拍摄了莫斯科学生上舞蹈课的照片，以展示他们铁律般的纪律，并与轻松随意的美国学校进行对比。该杂志捕捉了来访的苏联民间舞者，并报道了赫鲁晓夫谴责好莱坞电影中的舞蹈、进而对西方文化作出评判的新闻。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "生活的许多方面都可以通过舞蹈来观察，从人们选择活动身体的方式、他们如何展现自己、如何相互联系、庆祝和交流。这里有真正的影像宝库等待去探索。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《生活：我们跳舞吧》由 Taschen 出版社出版。", "links": [{"text": "LIFE. article_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "L ife magazine launched in 1936. Its aim: to show the US the world, in pictures. At a time when television was still an experimental medium, a golden age of photojournalism brought the outside world into people’s homes. Life ran weekly until 1972, spanning a transformative time in US culture. Photographers were dispatched across the globe, covering wars, political manoeuvres, social trends, hemlines and Hollywood. article_text:
L ife magazine launched in 1936. Its aim: to show the US the world, in pictures. At a time when television was still an experimental medium, a golden age of photojournalism brought the outside world into people’s homes. Life ran weekly until 1972, spanning a transformative time in US culture. Photographers were dispatched across the globe, covering wars, political manoeuvres, social trends, hemlines and Hollywood. And in December 1936, the magazine dedicated its cover feature to dance, with dancers from the new School of American Ballet gracing the front page. As such a vividly visual medium, dance would become a regular feature in Life’s pages across the years. When I was asked to write the text for a new book featuring a collection of dance-themed images from the Life archive, it was a kid-in-a-candy-shop situation. For a dance fan there were some absolute gems to be found: the great George Balanchine crafting his ballet The Seven Deadly Sins – and cooking dinner in his Manhattan apartment; Margot Fonteyn and Rudolf Nureyev taking New York in a piece headlined The Hottest Little Team in Show Biz; or an ageing Agnes de Mille going full-throttle in rehearsal.

But the archive told a much bigger story than that. It was fascinating to see the reflection of society through the way people danced: in ballrooms, nightclubs, proms and parties. In the array of social dancers: from the waltz and tango to the lindy hop, mambo, twist and the frug, themes of the 20th century play out. You can see a story of growing individualism in the shift from structured couple dancing to going freeform on the dancefloor – gender politics, too, as it was out with “May I have this dance?” and in with the democracy of the disco. Life columnist Albert Goldman asked: “Has there ever been a decade for dance like the 60s?” as he wrote of a power shift from the stage to the dancefloor, from the professional performer to the “inventive amateur”. There’s the birth of the teenager, too, bringing an explosion of pop culture and spreading dance trends on TV shows such as American Bandstand.

The archive also tells a story of the US’s shifting relationship with race, showing dancers in segregated bars and newly desegregated schools. But more than that, we see the way music and dance styles from Black communities and from Latin America were adopted, appropriated and absorbed into the US mainstream, whether tap, jazz, Charleston or cha-cha-cha.

Dance even had something to say about cold war politics and paranoia. For a series comparing American and Soviet education systems, which found the US lagging worryingly behind, Life took photos of Moscow students in a dance class to demonstrate their iron-clad discipline, compared with easygoing American schools. The magazine captured visiting folk dancers from the USSR, as well as reporting on Khrushchev denouncing the dancing in a Hollywood film, and by extension, casting judgment on western culture.

So much of life can be observed through dance, in the ways people choose to move their bodies and how they display themselves, how they relate to each other, celebrate and communicate. There’s a real treasure trove of images to explore.

LIFE. Let’s Dance is published by Taschen.

Step back in time: six pictures from Let’s Dance

On the set of Can-Can, 1959 (main image) The sheer raucous joy in this picture of Shirley MacLaine and Juliet Prowse leaps off the page, captured on the set of movie musical Can-Can, the story of a Belle Époque Paris cabaret whose dancers are arrested for public indecency. It was a stance approved of by Soviet premier Nikita Khrushchev, who was visiting the 20th Century Fox studios during filming and pronounced the dance routines depraved.

Willa Mae Ricker and Leon James, 1943 Ricker and James were members of Whitey’s Lindy Hoppers, one of the finest, and most awesomely acrobatic, dance troupes of the 1940s. The lindy hop originated among Black dancers in the clubs of Harlem (it was named after pilot Charles Lindbergh’s “hop” over the Atlantic in 1927) but by 1943, Life was calling the lindy hop “America’s national dance”.

The Rockettes, 1958 Modelled on high-kicking British group the Tiller Girls, all-American precision dance troupe the Rockettes took things up a notch with their machine-tooled synchrony. Launched in 1925, they’re still going strong today, proving the enduring allure of the showgirl (Taylor Swift can’t be wrong), and have even trademarked their signature dance technique.

Margot Fonteyn and Rudolf Nureyev in La Bayedère 1965 It is hard to imagine now that two ballet dancers could be as famous as Margot Fonteyn and Rudolf Nureyev were in the 1960s. Rudimania peaked on the Royal Ballet’s 1965 tour to the US, when mounted police were stationed outside New York’s Metropolitan Opera House to save Nureyev from being mobbed.

School prom, 1967 Teens dancing at the annual prom at Central High School in Little Rock, Arkansas. Ten years earlier, after the supreme court had ruled against segregation in public education, Arkansas’ governor called up the National Guard to stop nine Black students enrolling at the same school. Life’s journalist at the prom reported that “the school sees itself as desegregated rather than integrated”.

Michael Caine on the dancefloor, 1966 Such a keen dancer he was once known as Disco Mike, here’s Michael Caine at an LA club. Decades later he gave a tutorial on doing the twist on Jonathan Ross’s chatshow, a dance craze that had swept the world, meriting a seven-page feature in Life in 1961. From hipsters to socialites to suburban grandmas, everyone was caught up in “pulsating, gyrating, hip-swinging mania”, it reported.

article_text:
The Blood Countess de Ulrike Ottinger (film d’ouverture)

Isabelle Huppert en comtesse sanglante ? C’est la promesse de The Blood Countess , lubie baroque d’Ulrike Ottinger ( Aller Jamais Retour , 1979), figure anticonformiste de l’avant-garde queer allemande. Dans la Vienne de la fin du XIXe siècle, une comtesse glaçante et sa servante rôdent en quête de leur prochain repas. Entre icônes drag et créatures de la nuit, Huppert s’amuse avec Birgit Minichmayr et Conchita Wurst nous offre sa présence ardente. Une célébration queer des mythes sépulcraux.

Le mardi 17 novembre 2026 à 20h30 au MK2 Bibliothèque

La Bola Negra de Javier Calvo et Javier Ambrossi (film de clôture)

Prix de la mise en scène à Cannes 2026, La Bola Negra du duo « Los Javis » ( La Mesias , 2023) est l’une des fresques queer les plus flamboyantes de l’année ! Librement inspiré d’un texte de Lorca, le film connecte trois époques de l’Espagne à travers l’histoire de trois hommes queer confrontés aux mêmes épreuves, tous unis par la même volonté d’aimer. Dans cette œuvre ambitieuse et libératrice, Los Javis signent un hommage vibrant aux amours effacés de l’Histoire.

Le mardi 24 novembre 2026 à 19h30 au MK2 Bibliothèque

Du fioul dans les artères de Pierre Le Gall

Pour son premier long métrage, Pierre Le Gall convoque le génial Alexis Manenti ( Le Mohican ) aux côtés de Julian Swiezewski ( Brother ) dans un univers qui côtoie peu le désir et la douceur. Étienne, routier zélé, n’a que le fioul dans ses artères. Il se cantonne à de sommaires entrevues sur des parkings, jusqu’à sa rencontre avec Bartosz, routier lui aussi. Une romance queer pour le moins inattendue dans un milieu d’ordinaire viriliste, portée par deux acteurs qui font chavirer par leur naturalité.

le lundi 23 novembre 2026 à 16h00 au MK2 Beaubourg et le mercredi 18 novembre 2026 à 19h25 au MK2 Quai de Seine

En haut de la pile de Louis-Julien Petit

Ancré autour de l’homoparentalité, En haut de la pile de Louis-Julien Petit ( Les Invisibles , 2018) suit un couple éperdument amoureux, Maxime (Aliocha Schneider) et Arthur (Anthony Bajon), dans leur quête de fonder une famille. Leur désir de devenir pères croise un thème plus vaste sur la parentalité queer et les liens du sang. Épaulés par un formidable casting, avec Alexandra Lamy et Corinne Masiero en mères attentionnées, cette comédie sociale lumineuse nous interroge avec tendresse sur ce qui fait véritablement une famille.

Les Braves ( Coward ) de Lukas Dhont

Avec Les Braves (Coward) , le cinéaste belge Lukas Dhont ( Girl , Close ) signe son meilleur film et s’aventure pour la première fois dans un genre très éloigné de son univers délicat : le film de guerre. Porté par les révélations Emmanuel Macchia et Valentin Campagne, ce récit sensible et réaliste nous ramène en 1916 et suit Pierre, un jeune soldat belge envoyé au front durant la Première Guerre mondiale, qui se découvre au cœur du conflit et s’éprend de Francis, un artiste chargé de divertir les troupes.

le lundi 16 novembre 2026 à 19h45 au MK2 Quai de Seine

The Man I Love de Ira Sachs

Présenté en compétition à Cannes, The Man I Love signe le retour d’Ira Sachs ( Passages , 2023) dans le New York survolté des années 1980. Le film suit l’histoire de Jimmy, figure de la scène queer (interprété par Rami Malek), et son combat face à l’épidémie du VIH. Devant la fatalité de sa maladie, Jimmy choisit la soif de créer, de monter sur scène et d’aimer sans retenue. Conçu comme une fantaisie musicale retraçant le combat d’une communauté queer en lutte, ce récit dresse un portrait politique très émouvant, où l’art et l’amour deviennent de véritables actes de résistance.

le mardi 24 novembre 2026 à 13h50 au MK2 Beaubourg et le samedi 21 novembre 2026 à 20h10 au MK2 Quai de Seine

Roma Elastica de Bertrand Mandico

Dans Roma Elastica , Bertrand Mandico ( Les Garçons sauvages , 2017) convoque l’esthétique funky des eighties et le mélodrame baroque des grands cinéastes italiens. Une errance dans la Rome de 1982, où Marion Cotillard est Eddie, actrice américaine en perdition, accompagnée de sa maquilleuse Valentina (Noémie Merlant, toute de grâce), sur le tournage de son probable dernier film. Derrière ce décor se dessine une relation intime, portée par le magnétisme des deux actrices, comme un clin d’œil à l’heure de gloire de la Cinecittà, version 100 % queer.

le dimanche 22 novembre 2026 à 19h45 au MK2 Quai de Seine

Forty Love de Pierre-Ange Carlotti

Romeo Beckham fait ses tout premiers pas au cinéma dans Forty Love , le premier long métrage romantique et sensuel du photographe Pierre-Ange Carlotti. Il y donne la réplique à Paul Kircher ( Leurs enfants après eux ), qui incarne Sacha, un joueur entraîné par son père pour décrocher un titre à Paris. La naissance de cette rivalité vient bousculer sa carrière, transformant un duel passionnel en une histoire d’amour inattendue. Au casting également : Catherine Deneuve, Guillaume Canet et Benjamin Voisin.

le lundi 23 novembre 2026 à 19h55 au MK2 Quai de Seine

article_text:
Although Digger hasn’t performed well at the box office, the Alejandro G. Iñárritu film starring Tom Cruise is getting some high-profile positive reviews.

The satirical black comedy opened in theaters to an $8 million domestic debut , a $20M global start, and a C+ CinemaScore. Deadline reported that the film could lose around $150M .

However, the film has also gotten some reinforcement from Ben Affleck, Neil Young, Anne Hathaway, and Mandy Patinkin.

RELATED: 20 Great Films That Flopped At The Box Office From ‘Digger’ To ‘Fight Club’ And ‘Citizen Kane’

Ben Affleck recently defended Digger while appearing on the Happy Sad Confused podcast.

“It’s a little bit like the high-school bullying thing, with people who hadn’t even seen movies. You see it happening now, frankly, with Digger ,” the Animals actor said. “Everybody wants to celebrate this bomb as if it’s the most exciting thing to happen. And you think like, it’s a pretty ambitious, interesting movie made by interesting people who have talent.”

He continued, “Everybody wants to count the money, what it lost or whatever. To me, I just think, if you punish movies that take risks, guess what you’re going to get? A bunch of shitty homogenized movies. You cannot do something interesting without taking a big swing. And that means you’re going to sometimes look bad.”

RELATED: Anne Hathaway Calls Tom Cruise’s ‘Digger’ “Brilliant”: “It’s Worth Making The Time See & Decide For Yourself”

Neil Young wrote on his website to say that Digger is “the best film I have ever seen,” adding, “None of the reviews I have read describe this film adequately, in my opinion.”

“They seem to miss the overall effect, and most of them are negative,” he continued. “This film lives in a world of art. It is its own best review. Don’t read any other reviews and forget this one before you see Digger . It cannot be seen as a Tom Cruise film – that would be misleading. I would describe it as a film of our times… I do not view this film as a commercial venture. Rather it is an artful film of our times. The things that are said in Digger are a direct reflection of today’s political and social world. The film is so full of artful expression and radical change ups, that it may be too much to take in for those expecting a commercial film like we are used to today.”

RELATED: ‘Digger’ Delights ‘Homeland’ Star Mandy Patinkin: “One Of The Greatest Films I Have Ever Seen”

Scroll through the gallery below to see Hollywood’s positive reviews of Digger .

You see it happening now, frankly, with Digger,” the Animals actor said on the Happy Sad Confused pocast. “Everybody wants to celebrate this bomb as if it’s the most exciting thing to happen. And you think like, it’s a pretty ambitious, interesting movie made by interesting people who have talent.” He continued, “Everybody wants to count the money, what it lost or whatever. To me, I just think, if you punish movies that take risks, guess what you’re going to get? A bunch of shitty homogenized movies. You cannot do something interesting without taking a big swing. And that means you’re going to sometimes look bad.”

Neil Young Image Credit: Kevin Winter / Getty Images Neil Young wrote on his website to say that Digger is “the best film I have ever seen,” adding, “None of the reviews I have read describe this film adequately, in my opinion.” “They seem to miss the overall effect, and most of them are negative,” he continued. “This film lives in a world of art. It is its own best review. Don’t read any other reviews and forget this one before you see Digger. It cannot be seen as a Tom Cruise film – that would be misleading. I would describe it as a film of our times… I do not view this film as a commercial venture. Rather it is an artful film of our times. The things that are said in Digger are a direct reflection of today’s political and social world. The film is so full of artful expression and radical change ups, that it may be too much to take in for those expecting a commercial film like we are used to today.”

Anne Hathaway Image Credit: Mike Coppola / Getty Images The Verity star took to Letterboxd to praise the satirical comedy written and directed by Alejandro G. Iñárritu. “I loved this brilliant movie. It’s smart and trippy and aggressive and funny and ambitious,” Hathaway wrote on the social media platform. “It’s worth making the time see and decide for yourself what you make of it. For me? 10/10 🪏.”

Mandy Patinkin Image Credit: Dia Dipasupil / Getty Images Patinkin described Alejandro G. Iñárritu-directed Digger as an “instant classic” and said it was “one of the greatest pieces of film I have ever seen in my entire life.” “This is an incredible piece of work. It puts the heart and soul back into the cinema. Everything we all love about cinema, this is it. Please, please, please, run! Don’t walk, run, and see this film,” he continued.

article_text:
Tom Skerritt , the versatile actor who over his 60-plus year career played memorable roles in projects such as Top Gun , Picket Fences , M*A*S*H and Alien , has died. His family confirmed the actor passed away on October 21 from natural causes. He was 93.

Skerritt was often memorable in supporting roles for his quiet, powerful presence and infectious smile. On Picket Fences , however, he played the lead, Sheriff Jimmy Brock, and won an Emmy for the performance.

After a four-year stint in the Air Force, Skerritt gravitated first toward directing and later acting. His earliest roles included arcs on TV westerns such as The Virginian, Death Valley Days, 12 O’Clock High and Gunsmoke .

Among his first big screen roles was Captain Augustus Bedford “Duke” Forrest in Robert Altman’s 1970 big screen comedy, M*A*S*H . The character, who was Southern and came off as slightly racist, bunked with Hawkeye, Frank Burns and Trapper John and goes on to have an affair with Margaret “Hot Lips” Houlihan. Neither Skerritt nor his character appeared in the long-running TV spinoff. “I thought they would just make it into another sitcom,” he later told the Associated Press.

Skerritt later played Dee Mobley in his friend Altman’s 1974 film, Thieves Like Us .

Throughout the 1970s, Skerritt turned up in a number of big screen comedies, dramas and even a landmark sci-fi film. Those films included Harold and Maude , The Turning Point , Up in Smoke and Ice Castles . The sci-fi outing happened to be a film directed by a relatively new British director named Ridley Scott.

When Skerritt first got the script for Alien , he didn’t think much of it or his role as Dallas, the captain of the doomed ship, Nostromo . By the end of the shoot, however, the actor said he offered to trade his salary for half a percentage point on the film. “Ron Shusett, the executive producer, just laughed,” he remembered. He would reprise the character for the 2014 video game Alien: Isolation .

DEADLINE RELATED VIDEO:

The actor also worked continuously on TV throughout his decades-long career. During that period he appeared on The F.B.I., Mannix, Lancer and Hawaii 5-0 .

In 1986, Skerritt’s career hit another high point when he applied his Air Force experience as CDR Mike “Viper” Metcalf in Top Gun . A father figure to Tom Cruise’s Maverick, it’s Viper who tells Maverick the truth about his actual father’s heroic death. The conversation convinces a downcast Maverick to continue in the Top Gun program.

At about the same time, Skerritt had a recurring role on Season 6 of Cheers playing Evan Drake, a corporate boss, on whom Rebecca (Kirstie Alley) has a crush.

Skerritt got his breakout lead TV role on Picket Fences in 1992. The David E. Kelley-created show ran for four seasons on CBS. The drama is set in Rome, Wisconsin, a small town prone to odd occurrences which Skerritt’s Sheriff Jimmy Brock must investigate. While not a ratings blockbuster, Picket Fences garnered 14 Emmys, including Skerritt, who won Outstanding Lead Actor in a Drama Series in 1993.

After Picket Fences , Skerritt continued to work on top-tier shows, mostly in single-episode stints. A partial list of those titles includes Roseanne, Chicago Hope, Will & Grace, The West Wing, Law & Order: Special Victims Unit, The Closer, The Good Wife and Madam Secretary . He had multi-episode appearances on Huff, Brothers & Sisters and Leverage .

In 1992, Skerritt signed on to a film directed by Robert Redford, with whom he had co-starred in War Hunt way back in 1962. That film marked Skerritt’s big screen debut.

The impetus for their reunion was an adaptation of Norman Maclean’s wistful novella A River Runs Through It . The story follows the two sons of a Presbyterian minister as they come of age in Depression-era Montana. Skerritt played Rev. John Maclean with quiet authority. His sons, Norman and Paul, were played by Craig Sheffer and Brad Pitt, the latter in a performance that solidified his acting bona fides after his scene-stealing bit in Thelma & Louise . The film would go on to be nominated for three Oscars, winning for Best Cinematography.

Other prominent movie projects in the latter half of his career included Steel Magnolias, Singles, Contact and Smoke Signals .

Outside of Hollywood, Skerritt helped found TheFilmSchool in Seattle and the Red Badge Project, which helps veterans work through PTSD, anxiety and depression by writing and sharing their experiences.

{"type": "image", "url": "https://cdn.prod.tabdev.net/asset_files/uploaded/2026-10/274d6c99/83fd64db-7bcd-4c63-8e6e-3e6246ebd400.jpg?q=70&fm=webp", "alt": "", "caption": "真锅大度。特别举办的现场表演场景", "credit": "Tokyo Art Beat", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "真锅此前一直在YouTube上公开自己的实验影像，其起点可以追溯到大约20年前发布的一段肌电传感器测试视频。该内容通过肌肉收缩时产生的微弱电信号来控制外部设备，将身体当作乐器一样操控，伴随着让人联想到机器人舞的动作发出声响。本次展览的策展人是来自中国香港的微波国际新媒体艺术祭（Microwave International New Media Arts Festival）节目总监鄺佳玲（乔尔·邝）。她在真锅职业生涯早期于网络上偶然看到其实验影像并受到震撼，此后便一直关注他的创作。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "展览标题“RELATIONAL TIME - Life Beyond Simulation”包含了一种对比：机器可以在1秒内模拟出数千种未来，而人类建立信任与记忆却需要时间。这种“关系只有经过时间的沉淀才会诞生”的理念，成为了整个展览的基调。真锅本人对本次展览作出了如下评价：", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“在生成式AI迅速重塑智能与创造力的时代，艺术家们正面临着前所未有的质问。然而，人类的身体与神经系统却在截然不同的时间尺度上经历着生命。本次展览并非旨在将人类的知觉融化进机器的速度中；而是期望在保持彼此差异的同时，让我们的神经节奏与计算逻辑相互作用。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://cdn.prod.tabdev.net/asset_files/uploaded/2026-10/0e47d26f/07584f9c-41ce-4061-9a3b-959b6bdcc924.jpg?q=70&fm=webp", "alt": "", "caption": "真锅大度", "credit": "Tokyo Art Beat", "translated": "Tokyo Art Beat", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "作为展厅的台中市立美术馆位于由妹岛和世与西泽立卫（SANAA）设计的复合设施“台中绿美图”内。展厅层高在4m到10m之间，作品的音响系统全部从日本运来。日本、香港和台湾的团队经过反复的技术调试，将建筑空间本身作为展览的一部分融入其中。", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "15个AI通宵讨论资源分配方案", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在展厅A中，一个由单个细胞开始的人工生命世界投影在整面墙壁和地板上。画面中，散落着供细胞生存繁殖的营养——也就是所谓的“饵食”，这些营养在使用时会减少，随着时间推移又会恢复。细胞一边摄取这些饵食一边四处移动，不断重复着繁殖与死亡的过程。由于性质会从亲代传给子代，并不时发生变异，因此随着时间推移，会衍生出多个性质各异的细胞群。介入这个世界的并非人类，而是15个AI智能体。智能体们观察细胞的状况，讨论接下来应将大量饵食投放在何处，其中8个智能体根据各自不同的思路提出投放方案，6个智能体负责检查这些方案是否存在不合理或偏颇之处，最后的1个智能体则决定采纳哪一个方案。这是一个兼具提议者、检查者和最终决策者的类小型组织机制。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://cdn.prod.tabdev.net/asset_files/uploaded/2026-10/60f0df97/9614afb2-3cee-4184-b75d-737d9ee90911.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "展场风貌，整面墙壁和地板上投影着人工生命的世界", "credit": "Tokyo Art Beat", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "真锅过去也创作过人工生命作品，但他坦言，在设定好规则并由程序运行的基础上，靠自己的双手去调整饵食的投喂方式是最困难的环节。因此在本作中，真锅将自己决定的范围仅止于问题框架，而后续的调整则交由智能体之间的“讨论”来完成。讨论在夜间进行，结果则会反映在次日早上的展览中。会期长达约3个月，根据造访日期的不同能遇到不同的世界，这也是本次展览的趣味所在。", "translated": true}, "Tokyo Art Beat", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "影像的右侧显示的是智能体们的讨论记录，左侧则映衬出随着食物放置方式而不断分化的细胞群体。通过不把食物集中于1处、而是使其广泛分布，人们可以观察到多样化群体繁衍的过程。展厅内播放的音乐也是根据细胞的运动创作而成的。", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "参观者的动作改变着生物的世界", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "展厅B是一个被正面及左右3面屏幕环绕的空间。屏幕之中生活着数万只各类生物，它们寻找食物、与遇到的伙伴繁衍后代，并将亲代的特性传给下一代。这不是预先制作好的动画，而是根据生物之间的互动以及周边环境，其动作和数量都在一点点发生变化。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://cdn.prod.tabdev.net/asset_files/uploaded/2026-10/64cc3332/51d833e5-2900-4996-ab56-57a4c3109fa6.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "展场风貌，如颗粒般运动的生物上方叠加投影着AI的观察与调整记录", "credit": "Tokyo Art Beat", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "驱动这个世界的主要是3种力量。首先是参观者。展厅的传感器会读取诸如步行速度、驻足时间、人群是聚集还是分散等信息，并将其反映到画面的流动中。传感器无法识别个人，只能捕捉动作。当参观者移动时，流动随之改变，生物们的栖息地也随之转移。其次是生物自身的生命活动，进食、繁衍、诞生与死亡在不断重复。最后是由多个AI分工守护世界的、被称为“智能体群（Agent Swarm）”的机制。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://cdn.prod.tabdev.net/asset_files/uploaded/2026-10/37bf9383/3c52e1c7-410a-4c7e-97da-330d9d04790c.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "智能体将画面中的世界按区域分工，并以固定的间隔检查其状态。它们以确保生物不灭绝、保留多样物种、保持出生数与死亡数平衡以及引发变化为共同目标，一点点调整饵食数量和气候等条件，但并不直接操纵生物。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "参观者与生物、生物与AI之间的互动以各自不同的节奏同时推进。由于过去发生的事情所产生的影响会持续残留在世界中，因此在不同日期造访的人的动作，也将通过这个世界被连接起来。屏幕上交叠投影着如颗粒般运动的生物以及AI的观察与调整记录，这些变化也被转化成了展场的音效。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": Research和HHMI珍妮利亚研究所以及其他研究团队公开了一张详细记录黑腹果蝇大脑神经连接起点与终点的地图（连接组）。其中记录了大约16万7000个神经细胞以及连接它们的约1亿2500万处突触。真锅基于这张接线图，在计算机中构建出了人工大脑。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "3个展厅的共同点在于，作品并非以完成的状态放置在那里，而是作为一个随着时间推移不断变化的进程而存在。展厅A通过每晚的讨论、展厅B通过参观者的动作与智能体的介入、展厅C通过人与人工大脑的互动，分别以不同的速度改变着姿态。开幕之初与会期尾声所看到的风景必定会有很大差异，反复前往或许能发现更多平时看不到的东西。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "真锅谈到了在展场中聆听声音的意义以及会期中的计划：", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“我认为作品很大一部分只有在实际观看和聆听后才能传达出来。展厅中使用了各种各样的声音，比如大音量且精细控制的声音、旨在作用于身体的声音等。这次展览让我再次切身感受到，有些东西如果不去亲身体验是无法理解的。我正考虑在会期中举办表演，并推进相关准备工作，以便在我不在的时候也能通过播放录音的形式进行上演。我计划在11月和12月再次造访台中。”", "translated": true}, Beat", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "展会期间，还计划举行艺术家与策展人的对谈、引入不依赖视觉的欣赏方式与手语解说的包容性导览（Inclusive Tour），以及由当代表演艺术家担任导师的律动工作坊。", "translated": true}]

"heading", "text": "15体のAIが、資源の配り方を夜通し話し合う"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "展示室Aでは、たったひとつの細胞から始まる人工生命の世界が、壁と床いっぱいに映し出されている。画面の中には、細胞が生きて増えるための栄養、いわば \"エサ\"が場所ごとに散らばっていて、使われると減り、時間が経つとまた回復する。細胞はこのエサを取り込みながら動き回り、増えたり死んだりを繰り返す。親から子へ性質が受け継がれ、ときどき変化も起きるため、時間が経つにつれて性質の違う細胞のグループがいくつも生まれていく。 この世界に手を加えるのは、人間ではなく15体のAIエージェントだ。エージェントたちは細胞の様子を見ながら、次にどこへエサを多く置くかを話し合い、8体がそれぞれ違う考え方からエサの置き方を提案し、6体がその案に無理や偏りがないかを確かめる。そして、最後の1体がどの案を採用するかを決める。意見を出す人、チェックする人、最終判断をする人がそろった、小さな組織のような仕組みとなっている。"}, Art Beat"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "この世界を動かしているのは、大きく分けて3つの力だ。ひとつめは来場者。会場のセンサーが、歩く速さや立ち止まっている時間、人が集まっているか散らばっているかといった情報を読み取り、画面の中の流れに反映させる。センサーは個人を見分けず、動きだけをとらえる。来場者が動くと流れが変わり、生き物たちの居場所も動いていく。ふたつめは生き物たち自身の営みで、食べる、子孫を残す、生まれる、死ぬといったことが絶えず繰り返されている。3つめが、何体ものAIが手分けして世界を見守る「エージェント・スウォーム」と呼ばれる仕組みだ。"}, ResearchやHHMIジャネリア研究所などの研究チームが、ショウジョウバエの脳の神経がどこからどこへつながっているかを細かく記した地図（コネクトーム）を公開した。そこには約16万7000個の神経細胞と、それらを結ぶ約1億2500万ヶ所のつながりが記録されている。真鍋はこの配線図をもとに、コンピュータの中で動く人工の脳を組み上げた。"}, {"type": "image", "url": "このハエの脳には、目も脚もない。その代わりに会場のセンサーが目の役割を果たし、来場者の動きを刺激として人工の脳に届ける。刺激は脳の中の神経を次々と伝わっていき、その反応が音や光、映像になって現れる。天井の24ヶ所からは音と光の粒が生まれ、部屋の中央にある4面のディスプレイには、脳の中で神経が反応していく様子が映し出される。"}, {"type": "image", "url": Beat"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "聞こえてきた音に反応して来場者がまた動くと、それが新しい刺激となって次の音が鳴る。会場で流れる音楽は、その場にいる人の動きによって刻々と変わっていくため、同じ演奏を2度聴くことはできない。"}, {"type": "heading", "text": "会期中も姿を変え続ける3つの部屋"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "3つの展示室に共通しているのは、作品が完成した状態で置かれているのではなく、時間の経過とともに変化していくプロセスとして存在している点だ。展示室Aは夜ごとの議論によって、展示室Bは来場者の動きとエージェントの介入によって、展示室Cは人と人工の脳とのやりとりによって、それぞれ異なる速さで姿を変えていく。開幕直後と会期終盤とでは目にする風景も大きく違ってくるはずで、繰り返し足を運ぶことで見えてくるものもあるだろう。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "真鍋は、会場で音を聴くことの意味と、会期中の予定について次のように語った。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "「作品は実際に見て、聴いてもらうことではじめて伝わる部分が大きいと思います。会場では、大音量で細かく制御した音や、身体に働きかけるための音など、様々な音を使っています。体験してもらわなければわからないものがあるということを、今回の展示であらためて実感しました。会期中にはパフォーマンスを検討していて、私が不在のときでも録音を再生するかたちで上演できるよう準備を進めています。11月と12月には、また台中を訪れたいと考えています」"}, article_text:
人と機械、それぞれの時間を重ねる。真鍋大度が台中で開く初の海外大型個展

台湾の台中市立美術館で、真鍋大度の個展「RELATIONAL TIME - Life Beyond Simulation（關係時態：超越模擬的生命形式）」が開幕した。会期は2027年1月3日まで。真鍋にとって初となる海外での大型個展で、同館の3つの展示室それぞれに合わせた新作を展示している。人工生命、AIエージェントの集団、ショウジョウバエの神経回路という異なる素材を扱いながら、どの部屋も訪れるたびに違う姿を見せる。

1976年、東京生まれの真鍋大度は、大学で数学を学ぶかたわら、プログラミングやDJの活動を始めた。その後、情報科学芸術大学院大学（IAMAS）で音楽と音響設計を学び、のちに長く協働することになる石橋素と出会う。2006年にはライゾマティクスを設立し、坂本龍一やPerfume、ビョークとの共作、リオデジャネイロ大会の閉会式で行われた東京への引き継ぎセレモニーなど、ポップカルチャーと先端技術の両方にまたがる仕事を手がけてきた。

真鍋は以前から自身の実験映像をYouTubeで公開しており、その始まりは約20年前に投稿された筋電センサーのテスト動画にさかのぼる。筋肉が収縮するときに生じる微弱な電気信号で外部の機器を動かし、身体を楽器のように扱うという内容で、ロボットダンスを思わせる動きに合わせて音が鳴っていく。本展のキュレーターを務めるのは、香港の微波国際新媒体芸術祭（Microwave International New Media Arts Festival）のプログラムディレクター、鄺佳玲（ジョエル・クォン）。キャリアの初期にネット上で真鍋の実験映像に出会って衝撃を受け、以来その活動を追い続けてきたという。

展覧会のタイトル「RELATIONAL TIME - Life Beyond Simulation」には、機械が1秒で数千通りの未来をシミュレーションできるのに対し、人間が信頼や記憶を築くには時間がかかるという対比が込められており、関係は時間をかけてはじめて生まれるという考えが展示全体の土台になっている。真鍋自身は本展について次のように語っている。

「生成AIが知性や創造性を急速に塗り替えていく時代に、アーティストはかつてない問いに直面しています。しかし人間の身体や神経系は、コンピュータの処理とはまったく異なる時間のスケールを生きています。この展覧会は、人間の知覚を機械の速度に溶け込ませるためのものではありません。互いの違いを保ったまま、私たちの神経のリズムと計算のロジックを作用させ合うことを目指しています」

会場となる台中市立美術館は、SANAAが設計した複合施設「台中緑美図」の中にある。展示室の天井高は4mから10mにおよび、作品の音響システムはすべて日本から運び込まれた。日本、香港、台湾のチームが技術面の調整を重ね、建築空間そのものを展示の一部として取り込んでいる。

15体のAIが、資源の配り方を夜通し話し合う

展示室Aでは、たったひとつの細胞から始まる人工生命の世界が、壁と床いっぱいに映し出されている。画面の中には、細胞が生きて増えるための栄養、いわば "エサ"が場所ごとに散らばっていて、使われると減り、時間が経つとまた回復する。細胞はこのエサを取り込みながら動き回り、増えたり死んだりを繰り返す。親から子へ性質が受け継がれ、ときどき変化も起きるため、時間が経つにつれて性質の違う細胞のグループがいくつも生まれていく。 この世界に手を加えるのは、人間ではなく15体のAIエージェントだ。エージェントたちは細胞の様子を見ながら、次にどこへエサを多く置くかを話し合い、8体がそれぞれ違う考え方からエサの置き方を提案し、6体がその案に無理や偏りがないかを確かめる。そして、最後の1体がどの案を採用するかを決める。意見を出す人、チェックする人、最終判断をする人がそろった、小さな組織のような仕組みとなっている。

真鍋は、これまでも人工生命の作品を作ってきたが、ルールを決めてプログラムで動かしたうえで、エサの与え方を自分の手で調整する作業がいちばん難しかったという。そこで本作では、真鍋が決めるのは問題の枠組みまでとし、その先の調整はエージェント同士の"話し合い"に任せた。話し合いは夜のうちにおこなわれ、結果は翌朝の展示に反映される。会期は約3ヶ月と長く、訪れる日によって違う世界に出会えるのも本展の面白さのひとつだろう。

映像の右側にはエージェントたちの話し合いの記録が、左側にはエサの置き方によって細胞の集団が分かれていくところが映し出される。エサを1ヶ所に集めず広く行き渡らせることで、多様な集団が育っていく過程を見ることができる。会場に流れる音も、細胞の動きをもとに作られている。

来場者の動きが、生き物たちの世界を変える

展示室Bは、正面と左右の3面スクリーンに囲まれた空間だ。スクリーンの中では何種類もの生き物が数万匹暮らしていて、エサを探し、出会った相手と子孫を残し、親の性質を次の世代へ伝えている。あらかじめ作られたアニメーションではなく、生き物同士の関わりや周りの環境によって、動き方も数も少しずつ移り変わる。

この世界を動かしているのは、大きく分けて3つの力だ。ひとつめは来場者。会場のセンサーが、歩く速さや立ち止まっている時間、人が集まっているか散らばっているかといった情報を読み取り、画面の中の流れに反映させる。センサーは個人を見分けず、動きだけをとらえる。来場者が動くと流れが変わり、生き物たちの居場所も動いていく。ふたつめは生き物たち自身の営みで、食べる、子孫を残す、生まれる、死ぬといったことが絶えず繰り返されている。3つめが、何体ものAIが手分けして世界を見守る「エージェント・スウォーム」と呼ばれる仕組みだ。

エージェントたちは画面のなかの世界を区域ごとに分担し、決まった間隔で状態を確かめる。生き物が絶滅しないこと、いろいろな種類が残ること、生まれる数と死ぬ数のバランスを保つこと、変化を起こすことを共通の目標にして、エサの量や気候などの条件を少しずつ調整する。しかし、生き物を直接動かすことはしない。

来場者と生き物、生き物とAIのやりとりは、それぞれ違うペースで同時に進んでいる。前に起きたことの影響はその後も世界に残り続けるため、別の日に訪れた人の動きも、この世界を通じてつながっていく。スクリーンには、粒のように動く生き物たちと、AIによる観察や調整の記録が重ねて映され、その変化は会場の音にも置き換えられる。

真鍋によると、この部屋の映像の見せ方は、AIエージェントたちが毎週新しく作り替えているという。AIは来場者の動きのデータをもとに話し合い、そのためのプログラムを自分たちで書いている。中央の画面には、その話し合いの内容とできあがったプログラムが映し出され、AIが人の動きをどう読み取り、映像に変えたのかという過程までたどることができる。

ハエの脳の配線図が、人の動きを音楽に変える

真鍋はこれまでも、脳や神経を使って音楽や映像を生み出す実験を続けてきた。自分自身の脳の活動の計測から、ラットの神経細胞、人のiPS細胞から育てた小さな脳のかたまり（脳オルガノイド）まで、その方法は様々だ。会場で真鍋は、もともと自分の脳を書き換えてみたいという思いがあったと振り返る。ただ、人間の脳は簡単に開くことができず、生きた細胞を扱う実験には苦労も多かったという。

展示室Cで使われているのは、生きた細胞ではなく、ハエの脳の配線図だ。今年、Google ResearchやHHMIジャネリア研究所などの研究チームが、ショウジョウバエの脳の神経がどこからどこへつながっているかを細かく記した地図（コネクトーム）を公開した。そこには約16万7000個の神経細胞と、それらを結ぶ約1億2500万ヶ所のつながりが記録されている。真鍋はこの配線図をもとに、コンピュータの中で動く人工の脳を組み上げた。

このハエの脳には、目も脚もない。その代わりに会場のセンサーが目の役割を果たし、来場者の動きを刺激として人工の脳に届ける。刺激は脳の中の神経を次々と伝わっていき、その反応が音や光、映像になって現れる。天井の24ヶ所からは音と光の粒が生まれ、部屋の中央にある4面のディスプレイには、脳の中で神経が反応していく様子が映し出される。

聞こえてきた音に反応して来場者がまた動くと、それが新しい刺激となって次の音が鳴る。会場で流れる音楽は、その場にいる人の動きによって刻々と変わっていくため、同じ演奏を2度聴くことはできない。

会期中も姿を変え続ける3つの部屋

3つの展示室に共通しているのは、作品が完成した状態で置かれているのではなく、時間の経過とともに変化していくプロセスとして存在している点だ。展示室Aは夜ごとの議論によって、展示室Bは来場者の動きとエージェントの介入によって、展示室Cは人と人工の脳とのやりとりによって、それぞれ異なる速さで姿を変えていく。開幕直後と会期終盤とでは目にする風景も大きく違ってくるはずで、繰り返し足を運ぶことで見えてくるものもあるだろう。

真鍋は、会場で音を聴くことの意味と、会期中の予定について次のように語った。

「作品は実際に見て、聴いてもらうことではじめて伝わる部分が大きいと思います。会場では、大音量で細かく制御した音や、身体に働きかけるための音など、様々な音を使っています。体験してもらわなければわからないものがあるということを、今回の展示であらためて実感しました。会期中にはパフォーマンスを検討していて、私が不在のときでも録音を再生するかたちで上演できるよう準備を進めています。11月と12月には、また台中を訪れたいと考えています」

会期中には、アーティストとキュレーターによるトーク、視覚に頼らない鑑賞や手話による解説を取り入れたインクルーシブツアー、コンテンポラリーのパフォーマンスアーティストが講師を務めるムーブメントワークショップも予定されている。

article_text:
Die Art Basel Paris wurde wegen bevorstehender Proteste abgebrochen, die Art Cologne schwankte zwischen Krise und Aufbruch. In dieser Folge des Monopol-Podcasts fragen wir, wohin es mit dem Format Kunstmesse geht

Das Format der Kunstmesse wurde immer mal wieder totgesagt; zuletzt während der Corona-Pandemie, als es kurzzeitig so aussah, als könne man jede Form von Shopping einfach ins Internet auslagern. Ganz so kam es aber nicht, und so war auch dieser Kunstherbst von Messen geprägt, allen voran der Art Basel in Paris und der Art Cologne in Köln.

In der französischen Hauptstadt wurde das schicke Schaulaufen im Grand Palais allerdings vorzeitig beendet, da neue Ausschreitungen am Rande der aktuellen Protestbewegung befürchtet wurden und auch die vermögende Sammlerschaft auf der Art Basel zum Feindbild der Demonstrierenden wurde. Im Podcast "Kunst und Leben" spricht Monopol-Chefredakteurin Elke Buhr über ihre Erfahrungen in Paris und die Widersprüche und Ungleichheiten, die schon immer Teil des Kunstbetriebs waren und im Moment besonders deutlich hervortreten.

Ein wenig bescheidener ging es in Köln zu , wo in Gestalt von Wolfram Weimer zum ersten Mal ein Kulturstaatsminister die Art Cologne eröffnete . Hier ging es unter anderem um die Frage, wie besonders kleinere Galerien mit dem wirtschaftlichen Druck umgehen können, der auf ihnen lastet, und wie eine neue Sammlergeneration zum Kunstkaufen animiert werden kann.

Elke Buhr und Monopol-Redakteurin Saskia Trebing haben sich dazu in Köln umgehört und erzählen im Podcast von einem vorsichtigen Optimismus, der ihnen begegnet ist. Auch der Art-Cologne-Leiter Daniel Hug kommt zu Wort und erklärt, warum Flexibilität und kleinere Stände die besten Möglichkeiten einer Messe sind, um Galerien zu unterstützen. Kristian Jarmuschek, Vorsitzender des Bundesverbandes Deutscher Galerien und Kunsthändler e. V., ist überzeugt, dass es Kunstmessen auch noch in 100 Jahren geben wird. Das analoge Erleben von Werken und der persönliche Kontakt zu Menschen seien durch nichts zu ersetzen.

article_text:
The week around the world in 20 pictures

Students win the election in Serbia, Flávio Bolsonaro flees Brazil, a train crash in Spain and Obama on the midterm campaign trail – the past seven days as captured by the world’s leading photojournalists

Warning: this gallery contains images some readers may find distressing

Fri 30 Oct 2026 16.10 EDT

Urda, Spain

Spain began three days of mourning on Thursday for at least 69 people who died in the crash, as dozens of injured passengers remained in hospital. Train drivers went on strike to urge more investment in railway safetyPhotograph: Manu Fernández/AP

Kyiv, Ukraine

damaged a university campus and Kyiv’s important Southern Bridge on Tuesday night, in what Volodymyr Zelenskyy described as ‘a serious escalation’ against Ukrainian infrastructurePhotograph: Genya Savilov/AFP/Getty Images

Kharkiv, Ukraine

they described as a ‘frank and substantive’ phone call with

Vladimir Putin this week about efforts to end the warPhotograph: Sergey Kozlov/EPA

Belgrade, Serbia

The concession ushered in a seismic political shift after a historic election that saw the increasingly authoritarian leader pitted against a student-led movement that had spent two years protesting against his governmentPhotograph: Uros Arsic/Reuters

Belgrade, Serbia

who flocked to the students’ final pre-election rally last week in Belgrade, fuelled early speculation that the students may have gained enough support

to launch a new political era in the Balkan country Photograph: Marko Drobnjaković/AP

Orléans, France

conviction for embezzlement of European parliament funds , promised to

‘bring back order to France’ Photograph: Alain Jocard/AFP/Getty Images

Brasília, Brazil

Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva brought

rapturous supporters on to the streets , while also thrilling conservationists, climate activists and social justice campaigners across the worldPhotograph: Evaristo Sa/AFP/Getty Images

Miami, Florida, US

Bolsonaro declared himself the ‘true president’ of Brazil after losing the presidential election and fleeing to the US, even though his own party has recognised the legitimate victory of

Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva , as have all of Brazil’s institutions and international observers who monitored the votePhotograph: Joe Raedle/Getty Images

Detroit, Michigan, US

‘fighting for change, real change, that will get money out of politics and put money in your pocket’ , as he threw his weight behind the Democratic candidatePhotograph: Paul Sancya/AP

Maracay, Venezuela

Trump administration had reportedly opposed Machado’s return, believing

her presence would complicate the cosy relationship it has struck up with the interim president, Delcy Rodríguez, since abducting the former leader Nicolás Maduro in JanuaryPhotograph: Gaby Oráa/Reuters

Hebron, West Bank

Netanyahu’s far-right coalition lost its majority in the election after four years in power. The main Jewish opposition bloc also fell short, however, leaving two Arab Israeli parties, the Joint List and Ra’am,

holding the balance of power Photograph: Ilia Yefimovich/AFP/Getty Images

Jerusalem

Netanyahu has been accused of using smear tactics to cling to power, after he claimed Arab Israeli parties had used foreign backing to ‘steal’ Tuesday’s electionPhotograph: Ohad Zwigenberg/AP

Gaza

by the struggle to find food and water to follow the Israeli election campaign . Fears of renewed hunger are mounting as markets run short of fresh produce and other essentialsPhotograph: Bashar Taleb/AFP/Getty Images

Alalak, Indonesia

Almost 2m hectares have gone up in smoke in Indonesia’s

worst fire season in a decade , enveloping the region in a thick dystopian hazePhotograph: Muda Sagala/AFP/Getty Images

Tirana, Albania

Albania has introduced fines of more than $6,000 for demonstrators who participate in a protest that turns violent, even if they don’t personally commit violent acts, as the government tries to clamp down on the rallies

calling for the prime minister’s resignation Photograph: Valdrin Xhemaj/Reuters

Paris, France

Hundreds of thousands marched in cities across France last Saturday in largely peaceful protests to support

schoolchildren’s demands for more teachers and repairs to dilapidated buildings, as Emmanuel Macron faces a social and political crisis in his final months as presidentPhotograph: Hannah McKay/Reuters

Paris, France

the government fast-tracks a bill to make protesters pay for damage caused by vandalism , even if they did not directly cause it themselvesPhotograph: Sameer Al-Doumy/AFP/Getty Images

Hardelot, France

Huntington Beach, California, US

Historic high tides have caused chaos up and down the California coast this weekPhotograph: Mario Tama/Getty Images

Fleetwood, England

hailed the club’s victory as one for all football after his side

shocked the Premier League champions on penalties. The side, currently 18th in League Two, held their nerve in the shootout, with Conor Haughey hitting the winner to reach the quarter-finalsPhotograph: Jon Super/Reuters

article_text:
Savannah College of Art and Design has completed its SCAD Film Studios expansion in Savannah, Georgia.

The 16-acre complex of SCAD Savannah Film Studios added new professional soundstages and more than 50 backlot facades and practical interiors to Savannah’s production landscape. The space, built for professional productions as well as students, is the largest university film studio complex in the world.

Related Stories

‘I’m Still Here’ Star Maeve Jinkings Set for Women’s Convent-Prison Daring Escape Drama ‘Cabildo 71’ (EXCLUSIVE)

Ventana Sur Proyecta 2026: A Powerhouse New Generation Lineup Backed by Some of Latin America’s Finest Producers

SCAD Film Studios is designed to welcome professional productions while giving students opportunities to work alongside experienced crews, performers and creative leaders.

Andra Reeve-Rabb, dean of the SCAD School of Film and Acting, executive director of SCAD Casting, said, “At SCAD, we don’t wait for students to graduate to introduce them to the entertainment industry.” She added, “We bring the industry directly to them. We’ve built a place where a major production can come to Savannah and find everything it needs — professional soundstages, an extraordinary backlot, cutting-edge technology and talented emerging artists ready to contribute.

“Our students aren’t watching the industry from the sidelines. They’re working alongside the professionals who will become their future colleagues. That’s an ‘only at SCAD’ experience.”

At the center of the expansion is a Hollywood-style backlot featuring more than 50 façades and versatile filming environments that can transport productions from historic Savannah to New York City streets or small-town America.

The backlot includes brownstones, storefronts, restaurants, urban alleyways, a subway entrance, and a suburban neighborhood, with practical interiors that allow filmmakers to move seamlessly between exterior and interior scenes.

The final phase also includes two purpose-built professional soundstages of nearly 9,000 square feet. These stages, along with the 17,000-square-foot production design and costume design building, help support all components of the creative process.

The studios are already attracting high-profile entertainment projects. Leslie Odom, Jr., who recently joined SCAD as an artist-in-residence alongside actor and singer Nicolette Robinson, will develop and rehearse his upcoming national holiday tour on one of the new soundstages. SCAD students are helping build sets for the production and will gain firsthand exposure to the creative and rehearsal process as Odom prepares for his Nov. 27-Dec. 22 tour.

“American Idol” is also utilizing SCAD Film Studios facilities, creating another connection between professional entertainment production and the university’s emerging talent. The project’s use of SCAD’s production resources reflects the complex’s ability to accommodate major television productions while creating opportunities for students across disciplines, from acting and on-camera performance to production design and behind-the-scenes work.

The Savannah expansion is complemented by SCAD Film Studios in Atlanta, which includes an additional LED volume stage, broadcast studios and editing facilities.

King）在这部令人作呕的惊悚片练习中饰演她自己，或者说是一种带有准虚构色彩的自己。片中引发反感情绪的，不一定是最后卷轴中爆发的最终血腥场面，而是那种庸俗诡异的方式——影片模仿了社交媒体短视频和流媒体废话的种种做派，既讽刺了这一行业的丑陋一面，又同时对其进行剥削并从中牟利。从某种层面来看，这是一场极其聪明的不诚实练习，就像一部专为Z世代刺激感而拍的劣质迈克·哈内克电影（例如《趣味游戏》）；从另一个层面来看，它或许只是对那些早已过度曝光的网络老套路的拙劣山寨。或者两者皆有。", Baum und Pferdgarten 等潮流周边供应商的购物之旅，在当地高级餐厅的用餐，以及随后对“鬼屋”的直播访问——这也是如今 Instagram 和 TikTok 上的热门大事件。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": {"type": "paragraph", "text": "那么，我们是该因为基娅的贪婪而鄙视她，还是该为她不被跟踪狂吓倒的女强人坚韧精神鼓掌？而对于影片声称部分灵感来源于真实的跟踪骚扰事件，又该作何感想？尼布罗及其团队将这场争论融入了无休止的评论流中，这些评论随着基娅的直播不断滚动——这是一条即便在片尾字幕开始滚动时也未曾停歇的聊天河流，是数字泛滥时代的一种代用品证法。", article_text:
B ritish influencer/singer/content creator Chiara King stars as influencer/singer/content creator Chiara King, or some kind of parafictional version of herself, in this quease-inducing thriller exercise. The ick gets generated not necessarily by the eventual gore that erupts in the last reel, but by the tacky weirdness of the way the film apes the mannerisms of social media reels and streaming nonsense to both satirise the ugly side of the business but also exploit and profit off it at the same time. On one level, it’s an eerily clever exercise in bad faith, like a poor Michael Haneke film (think Funny Games) for gen-Z kicks; on another, maybe it’s just a crappy ripoff of online tropes that have been way overexposed already. Or both.

Anyway, here’s what happens: influencer Chiara gets invited to visit Copenhagen by a tourist organisation, a deal set up by her avaricious manager Alice (Jazmine Summer). Of course, this means practically every moment of her time awake in the city will be filmed, both by Chiara herself on her trusty smartphone, or a camera crew led by director Mike (played by Mike Nybroe, who is also director of The Influencer Project, ha ha); Mike is supported by sound man Daniel (Daniel Parmo) and cameraman Victor (Luca Storm). The early sections turn in all the influence-slop you would expect, with shopping trips to trendy merch vendors such as Baum und Pferdgarten, and meals at fancy local restaurants, and then a livestreamed visit to a “haunted house,” which is the big thing on Instagram and TikTok these days.

But the product placement is somewhat interrupted by moments of real fear (or “real fear”) when Chiara starts getting threatening direct messages (from someone calling themselves KingSlayer) who wants her to stop talking for reasons not clearly explained at first, otherwise he will kill and rape her, not necessarily in that order. This unsurprisingly creates a pall over Chiara’s trip, but if she just quits and goes home she’ll miss out on $100k in deals, so that’s not an option.

So are we supposed to despise Chiara for her greed or applaud her girl-boss fortitude in not being intimidated by a stalker? And what to make of the film’s claims that this was partly inspired by real incidents of stalking? Nybroe and co work the debate into the endless stream of comments we see scrolling alongside Chiara’s livestream – a river of chat that doesn’t let up even when the credits start to roll, ersatz dialectics for an age of digital proliferation.

article_text:
シャネルのアート誌第2号が刊行。シンディ・シャーマンの新作を多数収録、東京でも配布

シャネル が手がける雑誌『Arts & Culture Magazine』第2号が10月23日に刊行され、無料で配布される。表紙を飾る シンディ・シャーマン による多数の新作セルフポートレートや、 パティ・スミス の自筆の歌詞などが収録されている。

シャネル ・カルチャー・ファンドが、2025年夏に創刊した雑誌『Arts & Culture Magazine』の第2号を10月23日に刊行する。表紙を飾るのは、シャネルのツイードをまとったアーティスト、 シンディ・シャーマン だ。

約300ページからなる本誌には、シャーマンの新作セルフポートレートが多数収録されている。『 ヴァニティ・フェア 』によると、今回の制作にあたり、シャネルの歴史的資料を収蔵するパトリモワンヌ・アーカイブから、衣服に仕立てられる前のヴィンテージの布地がロール状で送られた。コスチュームジュエリーも提供され、シャーマンは布地を自ら裁断し、体に巻きつけるなどして、写真の中で演じる人物たちの衣装をつくり上げた。シャーマンは、アーカイブの布地を使うにあたり、「『切り刻んだり、穴を開けたりしてもいいんですか？』と聞いたんです」と同誌に語っている。

こうして生まれた写真作品の一部は、ロンドンのメイフェア地区にあるギャラリー、 ハウザー＆ワース で 展示されている 。展覧会は フリーズ・ロンドン に合わせて10月13日に開幕し、12月23日まで開催される。

このほか誌面には、 パティ・スミス による自筆の歌詞も掲載。ピュリツァー賞受賞劇作家のリン・ノテージ（Lynn Nottage）と、ロンドンのナショナル・シアターで芸術監督を務めるインドゥ・ルバシンガム（Indhu Rubasingham）が、物語を舞台でどう表現するかを語り合う。また、作家のアンドリュー・ダービン（Andrew Durbin）は、 ペギー・グッゲンハイム の生涯と後世に残した功績について考察する。グッゲンハイムをテーマにした展覧会「 Peggy Guggenheim in London The Making of a Collector 」は、ロンドンのロイヤル・アカデミー・オブ・アーツで11月21日に開幕する。

シャネルでアート、カルチャー、ヘリテージ部門のプレジデントを務めるヤナ・ピールは、次のように述べている。

「シャネル・カルチャー・ファンドの活動の核にあるのは、アイデアやアーティスト、そして新しいものを生み出すという、何にも代えがたい営みを大切に育むことです。『Arts & Culture Magazine』は、その実践の軌跡を残す場です。第2号の表紙を飾る人物として、シンディ・シャーマンほどふさわしい人はいません。彼女は50年にわたり、アイデンティティがどのようにつくられるのか、そして女性が自らの人物像を形づくるうえで持つ力を探究してきました」

「彼女の写真は、女性の力を肯定し、慈しむまなざしを通じて、現代の女性と、自らを変えていく自由を描き出しています。だからこそ、シャーマンが最新シリーズの着想を、創業者ガブリエル・シャネルと、彼女が残した魅力に満ちたアーカイブから得たことは、驚くべきことではありません」

同誌は、世界各地の独立系書店や雑誌専門店、一部の文化施設で無料配布される。配布先には、香港のACO Books、メキシコシティのCasa Bosques、ロンドンのRococo News & Magazines、パリの7Lなどが名を連ねる。日本では、 東京 ・銀座のシャネル・ネクサス・ホールで 配布される 。（翻訳：編集部）

article_text:
A24’s Elizabeth Holmes documentary “ You Can See Everything ” and DC’s comic book adaptation “ Clayface ” are vying for first place at the domestic box office, with each film on track to collect around $10.5 million over the weekend.

Although it’ll be a close call, “You Can See Everything” has the slight edge with $10.6 million while expanding to 3,242 venues in its third frame while “Clayface” looks just behind with $10.4 million from 3,478 theaters in its sophomore outing, according to respective studio estimates. (The final results will be tallied on Monday.) “You Can See Everything” is already a box office winner, but it would be quite a feat for the non-fiction film to ascend to No. 1 in its third weekend in theaters.

Related Stories

BAFTA Trustees Accused of Potentially Violating Charity Law Over Free Ceremony Tickets

“That’s a rare achievement for any film, let alone a documentary running more than three hours,” says Rentrak’s head of marketplace trends Paul Dergarabedian.

Overall, it was another painfully slow Halloween for cinema owners without any new releases, as well as the misfortune of the holiday landing on Saturday. When Halloween coincides with the weekend, families prefer to go trick-or-treating rather than visit their local multiplex. Revenues between Friday and Sunday amounted to roughly $60 million, marking one of the slowest weekends of the year, according to Rentrak. However, it’s an improvement from 2025’s Halloween weekend, which resulted in $49 million across all films, led by Colleen Hoover adaptation “Regretting You” and “Black Phone 2.”

“With costume parties, trick-or-treating and countless other Halloween activities, theaters were facing some pretty stiff competition for people’s time and attention,” Dergarabedian says.

“You Can See Everything” has been the fall season’s breakout hit with $63.88 million domestically to date. It has yet to be released at the international box office. With euphoric word-of-mouth and repeat viewings from audiences who are trying to process the stranger-than-fiction film, “You Can See Everything” is expected to leave theaters as one of the biggest documentaries in decades. And it will be very profitable for A24, which produced the nearly three-hour movie for $7 million.

“Clayface,” an R-rated origin story about the Batman villain, has generated $44.1 million in North America and $83 million globally. It’s shaping up to be a modest win for DC, having cost just $44 million to produce. That’s a much leaner price tag than DC’s other recent tentpoles, such as last year’s $225 million-budgeted “Superman” and July’s $175 million-budgeted “Supergirl.” The studio spent less on “Clayface” because the story is much darker than those family-friendly adventures, and because the character isn’t as well known compared to some of the company’s A-list superheroes. DC’s next big-screen endeavors will feature marquee names with next summer’s “Superman: Man of Tomorrow” and 2028’s “The Batman: Part II,” led by Robert Pattinson.

Laika’s stop-motion animated fantasy “Wildwood” remained at No. 3 with $7.5 million in its sophomore outing, a 39% drop. So far, the well-reviewed film has earned $25 million domestically and $35 million globally. Since “Wildwood” has a huge $100 million production budget (stop-motion animation is labor-intensive and can take several years to produce), the movie likely won’t turn a profit in its theatrical run.

Fourth place went to Black Bear’s offbeat romantic comedy “Wicker” with $4.1 million from 2,374 venues in its second weekend, a decline of just 28% from its debut. The film has earned $13.2 million domestically to date, a solid tally considering the low-budget project was acquired by Black Bear after Sundance for $2.5 million.

Paramount’s video game reboot “Street Fighter” rounded out the top five with $3.2 million in its third frame, another harsh 63% drop. The movie has grossed $53 million in North America and $91.9 million worldwide. Although “Street Fighter” is nearing the $100 million mark, it’s not close to breaking even or getting into the black. Legendary and video game developer Capcom co-financed “Street Fighter” for $82 million, and theater owners keep around half of ticket sales.

Elsewhere, Sony didn’t report grosses for the Jenna Ortega-led literary adaptation “Klara and the Sun” in what would have been the film’s second weekend of release. The film collapsed in its opening with $720,000 from 880 locations. The studio scaled back the theatrical footprint after critics derided the movie as “ calamitous ” and “ confoundingly awful .” Director Taika Waititi claimed he doesn’t read reviews but, in a recent social media post, he referred to critics of his work as “sad lost souls who couldn’t achieve their dreams of becoming artists.” The movie cost $20 million to make and will wind up in the red for Sony. It’s the studio’s second consecutive misfire after Aaron Sorkin’s “The Social Reckoning,” which left theaters with a paltry $9 million in North America and $17 million globally against a $30 million budget. Luckily, the studio’s losses on those films will be cushioned by two major winners, “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” (the third-biggest movie ever with $2.5 billion) and Zach Cregger’s “Resident Evil” reboot ($400 million).

In limited release, Sony Pictures Classics’s crime thriller “The Only Living Pickpocket in New York” cracked the top 10 with $1.7 million from 1,112 theaters. It has earned $2.1 million after one weekend in limited release. John Turturro stars in the awards hopeful, which revolves around a pickpocket master who struggles to keep up with the changing times — phones are trackable, wallets rarely have cash and guns are hiding in plain sight.

Meanwhile, Netflix’s Oscar contender “La Bola Negra” added $418,000 from 38 theaters. So far, the generation-spanning queer drama has earned $1.2 million as the streamer rolls out the film at a glacial pace. Also this weekend, Netflix released Peter Berg’s war drama “The Mosquito Bowl,” which brought back $455,000 from 349 locations — a much wider footprint than “La Bola Negra.”

article_text:
EXCLUSIVE: Sony Pictures has acquired live-action film rights to the bestselling comic book series D’Orc , with its author and illustrator Brett Bean attached to adapt for the screen.

The film plot is under wraps, but the comic book series marries swashbuckling humor with sprawling magical mythology and creatures wrapped in a gritty, action-driven fantasy adventure. Published by Image Comics, the series debuted earlier this year and became an instant bestseller Its first issue sold out before its release and is now on its eighth printing. Subsequent issues also have gone into multiple printings.

In addition to D’Orc , Bean is the author of the graphic novel series Zoo Patrol Squad, and the Muk ‘n’ Honey book series. As an illustrator, his work has contributed to the Dungeon Crawler Carl comic series, puppet designs for Jim Henson’s Creature Shop, and Marvel’s comic book series Rocket and Groot .

Watch on Deadline

Bean is represented by ChengCaplan Company, InkWell Management and Alexander Lawrence.

奈良美智が紫綬褒章を受章。「芸術は、必ずしも社会の役に立つことを証明しなくてもいい」

現代美術家の 奈良美智 が、2026年秋の紫綬褒章に選ばれた。奈良は受章への感謝を表す一方、メディアの取材に対し、権威と距離を置いてきた自身の姿勢や、効率や実用性では測れない芸術の価値について語った。

日本政府は11月2日付で、2026年秋の褒章受章者736人と25団体を発表した。紫綬褒章には、現代美術家の 奈良美智 らが選ばれた。発令は11月3日となる。

紫綬褒章は、科学技術分野の発明・発見や、学術、スポーツ、芸術文化の分野で優れた業績を挙げた人に贈られる。毎年、春は4月29日、秋は11月3日に発令され、過去には 石内都 （2013年）、 畠山直哉 （2015年）、 青木野枝 （2021年）、 鴻池朋子 （2023年）らが受章している。

奈良は11月2日、Xに「多額の寄付や社会貢献に贈られる紺綬褒章はずっと断り続けてきましたが、自分の続けてきた美術を評価していただいた紫綬褒章は感謝し謹んでお受け致します」と 投稿した 。

朝日新聞の メールインタビュー では、これまで作品を見てくれた人や、活動を支えてくれた人たちへの感謝を表する一方、世の中の常識や権威とは距離を置いて活動してきただけに、国から褒章を受けることに不思議な感覚があると明かした。

奈良はまた、誰かに認められることを目標に制作してきたわけではなく、流行や市場の求めるものよりも、自分の内側から生まれるものを大切にしてきたと説明。その姿勢も含めて評価されたのであればうれしい、と述べた。

さらに、今回の受章を機に制作や活動を変える考えはないとも語り、速さや効率、わかりやすさを求める社会にあっても、絵を描くことには、時間をかけたり、遠回りしたりする余地があっていいと続けている。

「芸術は、必ずしも社会の役に立つことを証明しなくてもいいと思うんです。むしろ、何でも役に立つかどうかで判断する社会の方が、少し心配です」

奈良の活動は、今後も国内外で展開される。2027年秋には、アメリカの サンフランシスコ近代美術館 （SFMOMA）で、北カリフォルニアでは初めて、その活動を包括的に紹介する大規模な回顧展が開催される予定だ。
